explanation: The right spinal lemniscus carries left-sided pain and temperature because spinothalamic tract fibers cross at their segmental level before ascending in the brainstem.
Dorsal column tracts are supplied by posterior spinal arteries (branches of vertebral artery) and radicular arteries from the aorta; all of these sources contribute.
Lumbar puncture is performed at L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace, below or above the L4 spinous process tip, safely avoiding the spinal cord.
Complete section above C5 causes quadriplegia because all descending corticospinal fibers are interrupted before they synapse with lower motor neurons.
In hemisection, ipsilateral findings include proprioception loss and UMN signs; A and B only captures these correctly; pain loss is contralateral.
Brown-Sequard shows ipsilateral LMN at the same level, NOT contralateral; this is the exception among the listed features.
UMN lesion causes Babinski positive (dorsiflexion), spasticity, hyperreflexia; options A-D describe LMN or normal findings.
LMN lesion causes marked muscle wasting; hypertonia, absent/increased reflexes, and Babinski are UMN features not seen in LMN.
Syringomyelia first causes bilateral pain and temperature loss because the central syrinx damages crossing fibers before affecting other pathways.
Hindbrain comprises medulla, pons, cerebellum, and fourth ventricle; crus cerebri is a midbrain structure (part of cerebral peduncle).
Brain stem = midbrain + pons + medulla; cerebellum (hindbrain) and cerebral aqueduct (ventricular) are excluded.
Cranial accessory nerve arises from nucleus ambiguus and joins vagus nerve; this is why cranial XI is functionally part of CN X.
Right spinal lemniscus carries pain/temperature from left body because spinothalamic fibers cross at the spinal level before ascending.
Posterior spinal arteries and radicular arteries both supply dorsal columns; all of the above (D) is correct.
L4 spinous process is the lumbar puncture landmark; L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace is used, below the conus medullaris.
Complete section above C5 causes quadriplegia (all four limbs); paraplegia requires thoracic lesion, hemiplegia requires cerebral lesion.
Hemisection produces ipsilateral proprioception loss (dorsal column) and UMN signs below; A and B only captures both correctly.
Brown-Sequard LMN at same level is ipsilateral, not contralateral; this makes D the exception among the statements.
UMN produces hyperreflexia, spasticity, and Babinski positive; normal plantar flexion (E) is not a UMN sign.
LMN lesion causes flaccid paralysis and marked muscle wasting; hypertonia, hyperreflexia, and Babinski are UMN signs.
Syringomyelia causes bilateral suspended sensory loss for pain/temperature; the expanding syrinx crosses pain fibers first.
Hindbrain = rhombencephalon = medulla + pons + cerebellum + fourth ventricle; crus cerebri is midbrain (mesencephalon).
Brain stem excludes cerebellum; cerebellum is a separate brain division connected to brain stem via three peduncles.
Cranial XI from nucleus ambiguus joins vagus nerve; spinal part from C1-C5 is separate, explaining the nerve's unique dual origin.
Spinal lemniscus carries contralateral pain and temperature after decussation at spinal levels.
Posterior spinal arteries (from vertebral) and radicular arteries supply dorsal columns; both contribute to dorsal column blood supply.
L4 spinous process is the anatomical landmark for lumbar puncture; needle inserted at L3-L4 or L4-L5 interspace.
